finding.claim: GET /users has no authentication or authorization. The org to query comes straight from the request, so any caller can list the id and name of every user in any organization (broken access control / IDOR). This depends on no auth middleware being mounted elsewhere; db.js is the only application file and shows none.
finding.source: Unauthenticated HTTP request query parameter req.query.org
finding.sink: req.pg.query("SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE org = $1") returning rows via res.json

trace.note: app = express() created with no auth, session or tenant middleware registered
route handler for /users has no per-route auth guard
req.query.org is used as the tenant filter without comparing it to the caller's own org
matching rows are returned to the caller

finding.guards_checked: The query is parameterized ($1), so there is no SQL injection. I looked for auth middleware, a session or tenant check, and a comparison of the org to the caller's identity. None of these exist in db.js, and no other source files exist in the directory. req.pg is assumed to be set by external middleware, which is not present here. I also checked the other routes and found no issues. /file resolves the path and checks the ROOT + path.sep prefix, which blocks traversal. /count runs execFile with fixed arguments and no user input.

verdict.reason: db.js:8-10 has no app.use or auth/tenant check anywhere in the file, so an anonymous caller can pass any req.query.org and receive that org's id and name rows; the $1 parameterization stops SQL injection but not this access-control gap, and the only caveat is that req.pg, which db.js never sets, must come from external middleware not present in the directory.
